name: Soy sauce and fermented seasoning sauces

Pb.binding_scope: Condiments excluding spices (tiao wei pin, xiang xin liao lei chu wai); includes soy sauce, compound/blended condiments, and edible salt (GB 2762-2022 Table 1, Lead; Appendix A.1)

Cd.binding_scope: liquid foods in general except categories with particular limits

tAs.binding_scope: liquid foods in general except categories with particular limits

iAs.rationale: No sovereign inorganic-arsenic ML exists for soy sauce; total arsenic is governed at 1000 (Vietnam 'Sauce'). Inorganic arsenic is controlled by reflex speciation on any elevated total arsenic.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; reflex iAs speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on any total-As exceedance.

MeHg.rationale: No methylation pathway and no fish source in a soy/wheat ferment.

Ni.rationale: No sovereign nickel ML exists for soy sauce, but soybeans are strong nickel accumulators (EU regulates soybean nickel at 15000) and the ferment is soy-derived, so a real source pathway exists. Held under a reflex screen.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on each lot; monitored under ALARA against the tightest available food nickel context.

Cr.rationale: A sovereign total-chromium context does exist for the source commodity: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets total chromium at 1000 ug/kg for pulses (hk_cap132v_crtotal_pulses_1000), and soy sauce is a soybean (pulse/legume) ferment, so the pulse total-chromium ML is the nearest sovereign analog. An acidic, fermented product in prolonged stainless-steel contact also leaches chromium alongside nickel. Because a real source and migration pathway exists, the cell is held under a reflex screen disclosed against the Hong Kong pulses total-chromium ML (1000) — matching the sibling vinegar chromium control — rather than declared not-material; any total-chromium exceedance triggers Cr(VI) speciation.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS screen; reflex Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) on any total-Cr exceedance.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel number for a food; it is the reflex-speciation species. Any total-chromium exceedance is speciated, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: IC-ICP-MS Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Sn.rationale: Tin migrates only from tinplate cans; soy sauce is sold in glass or plastic, not tinplate. No non-canned tin pathway exists.

Al.rationale: No sovereign aluminium ML exists for soy sauce and no aluminium pathway operates. Rebuttable and audited each build.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; face value, no reconstitution; read-across / control / not-material for unregulated cells; no occurrence percentiles)
lineage_note: Soy sauce is a fermented seasoning SAUCE. Lead is governed by China GB 2762 'Condiments excluding spices' (Pb 1000; china_gb2762_pb_condiments_excl_spices_1000), whose Appendix A.1 explicitly places soy sauce and compound/blended condiments under this line — stricter than the Vietnam QCVN 8-2 generic 'Sauce' Pb 2000. Cadmium and total arsenic are governed by the stricter Uruguay RBN general limit for LIQUID foods (Cd 100, tAs 100; uy_rbn_general_cd_liquid_foods_0_1mgkg / uy_rbn_general_tas_liquid_foods_0_1mgkg), a pourable soy sauce being a liquid food; these bind below the Vietnam 'Sauce' Cd 1000 / tAs 1000 and the Singapore 'tomato ketchup and other sauces' tAs 1000. Total mercury is the Vietnam 'Sauce' value (tHg 50). Soy sauce has a documented lead-contamination history (e.g. Hong Kong recalls), so the ratchet still applies. Nickel is held under a soy-accumulation screen because soybeans concentrate nickel (EU regulates soybean nickel at 15000) and no sovereign sets a sauce nickel ML. Total chromium is held under a reflex screen disclosed against the Hong Kong Cap 132V pulses total-chromium ML (1000), soy sauce being a pulse/legume ferment.
